messages:
elaine_support: Customer reports intermittent 502s, no obvious request_id in their client logs. They said it happened at ~2026-03-16T17:24Z. Asked what exact artifacts to send for an escalation.

mike_oncall: Thanks — quick checklist from support side: env (hosted/dedicated/private), SDK version, exact time window, and a minimal repro curl or HAR.

mike_oncall: If they can't find a request id, ask them to grab: debug token from Console, HAR (if browser), mobile debug logs (SDK), and a curl reproducer. I'll paste minimal steps below.

ashley_eng: Console -> Sessions -> search by user/email or IP -> open session -> Copy "Debug token" (button). That token lets us look up the server-side span even if the client log has no request id. Ask them to paste that token into the ticket as `DEBUG_TOKEN=<token>` (do not include secrets).

ashley_eng: Browser HAR steps (Chrome):
1) DevTools (F12) -> Network tab -> check "Preserve log".
2) Reproduce the failing request.
3) Right-click -> "Save all as HAR with content".
4) Tell them to filter for requests to `api.redwood.inference` (or their proxy host) and include the HAR file.

mike_oncall: Minimal curl reproducer to send (ask them to redact the API key before upload):
```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-RW-Client: acme-web" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-small","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -D response_headers.txt --output response_body.json
```
Tell them to attach `response_headers.txt` and `response_body.json`. If server returns a 502, the response headers often include our internal correlator header (see below).

ashley_eng: Mobile SDKs: enable debug logs and capture the SDK log lines around the failure.
- Android: enable `REDWOOD_SDK_LOG=DEBUG` or use our `Logger.setLevel(DEBUG)` call in the latest SDK.
- iOS: set `Client.shared.logLevel = .debug` (or enable verbose in the sample app).
Look for lines like: `rw_request_id=<hex>` or `x-rw-trace=<value>` in the logs. If present, copy that exact header value.

mike_oncall: If they sit behind a proxy/edge, ask them to capture the upstream headers. We're commonly correlating on `X-RW-Trace` / `X-RW-Session`. If those are present in response or proxy logs, include one full header value (it maps quickly to our traces).

ashley_eng: If they cannot send HARs (security policy) ask for a minimal reproduction: a curl with the same host, method, path and body + a short time window and the `User-Agent` and any `X-Forwarded-*` headers. That plus Console debug token is usually enough.

mike_oncall: Uploading the debug bundle: ask them to compress (zip) the HAR, SDK logs, `response_headers.txt`, and a short README.txt with time window + environment + SDK version. Then attach it to the ticket or upload via the incident portal.

tracebot: Automated helper: when you paste a `DEBUG_TOKEN=...` into the ticket, the bot will respond with an upload link and a one-click trace lookup. If you hit the bot, include the token in the first message.

ashley_eng: Example client log snippet to copy if they find it (please copy exact line):
`2026-03-16T17:23:54.123Z INFO rw.request sent id=0x4f3a2b X-RW-Trace=4f3a2b-161f7a user=acct-123`
We can search by `id=...` or `X-RW-Trace=...` from our side.

mike_oncall: Remind them to redact API keys. They can replace Authorization header with `Bearer <REDACTED>` or `REPLACE_WITH_KEY`.

elaine_support: I'll DM them a short template to paste back. Template: time window + env + SDK+version + debug token + attach HAR/curl + small README.

elaine_support: Quick internal checklist before escalation -> 1) Got `DEBUG_TOKEN`? 2) HAR or curl + headers? 3) SDK logs (if mobile)? 4) Proxy headers (if present)? 5) Time window and approximate request id placeholder? If yes to 1-4, escalate to eng with the upload link.

mike_oncall: One more tip: if they only have server-side NLB logs, ask for the exact request timestamp +/- 30s and the upstream target IP; we can stitch traces from that info but debug token speeds it up.

elaine_support: Thanks — sending the steps to customer now. :thumbsup:
